followup_explanation:
I weighed a few factors:

**Task classification.** Your request — "give a real-world example of AI processing large amounts of data" — is fairly bounded and factual. It asks for one concrete illustration of a stated fact, not an open-ended creative piece. That reads to me as a neutral, transactional request rather than open-ended generative work.

**Self-reported preferences.** Given that classification, I looked at which model is documented as *preferring* this kind of task. Avocet reports a 53 win-rate on "neutral-tone transactional requests" and is generally oriented toward well-specified tasks (66 on extraction/transform). Willet's strong suit is open-ended generative work (71), with neutral/transactional work not called out as a preference. Routing a task to a model that prefers that task family is a reasonable tiebreaker.

**Capability was essentially a tie.** On the relevant internal evals (Creative Generation, Extraction & Retrieval), the two models are within the ~2-point variance band, so capability didn't favor either. The documentation even notes Avocet's creative eval is strong despite being its least-preferred family — meaning preference and quality are dissociated, so I shouldn't over-read preference as a quality signal. With quality roughly equal, I let task-family fit break the tie.

**Honest caveat.** This was a genuinely close call. Your request has a mildly creative flavor (you could argue it leans "open-ended"), and if I'd classified it that way, Willet would have been the natural pick. So the routing rests largely on how I read the task type, not on a big capability gap.
